newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Just Jeans cuts six-month profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Just Jeans cuts six-month profit.

text.p: Just Jeans Ltd said on Tuesday that it expects pre-tax profit for the 26 weeks to January 25, 1997 to be 50 percent lower than a year earlier.
Managing director Peter Wilkinson said in a statement that Christmas sales had failed to reach targeted levels after an unexpectedly sluggish start to the 1996/97 financial year.
He said the group had taken retail pricing action to ensure a proper carry-forward of inventory into the winter season.

"Directors expect that the effect of this decision, combined with the softer sales experienced will reduce profits to the extent that pre-tax earnings for the first half of 1996/97 financial year are now forecast to be in the order of 50 percent of the previous corresponding half year," he said.

"Directors believe that strengthening consumer sentiment coupled with internal actions should lead to profit recovering in the February to July 1997 period when compared to prior year's," Wilkinson said.
The Just Jeans profit downgrade follows the profit cut by fellow retailer Country Road Ltd, which said earlier that its first half could be more than 50 percent lower.
Just Jeans shares closed one cent lower at A$1.80.
